title: cost: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Anita Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost by providing safe, automated defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, add a small set of validated quantization profiles, and wire unit-economics tooling into the autotune pipeline. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) autotune defaults for dynamic batching and cache TTLs based on workload shapes, 2) quantization profile YAMLs and runtime selection logic for common model families, and 3) unit-economics instrumentation and a lightweight CLI to surface cost delta estimates during rollouts. The goal is predictable, conservative defaults that reduce cost without degrading quality, plus tooling to make tradeoffs explicit for SREs and platform users. Changeset: - Add autotune scheduler that ingests recent request histograms and suggests per-route batch_size and batch_timeout defaults. - Introduce cache policy defaults and a conservative default TTL/eviction heuristic for prefix/KV caches. - Add three quant profiles (fp16, int8-qkra, int8-perf-safeguard) with model-family heuristics and compatibility checks. - Integrate unit-econ calc: per-token cost model, expected throughput, and estimated monthly savings. - Expose a CLI command 'redwood cost-simulate' and a console endpoint for previewing autotune suggestions. Backwards compatibility: all changes use feature flags and safe fallbacks to existing behavior. Rollout plan: behind feature flag 'cost-autotune-v2' with staged rollout (internal canary -> opt-in tenants -> default-on after 2 weeks of monitoring). Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4921) [x] autotune scheduler unit tests [x] e2e smoke test for batching/cache behavior [x] quant profile validation harness [x] CI performance microbenchmarks run [x] docs & console UI changes [x] release notes included Testing: unit and integration tests in CI; initial benchmarking showed median latency +2% on tail-critical routes but throughput improved 18% and cost per token reduced ~12% on our internal gen workloads. Observability: new metrics added: autotune.suggestions.count, autotune.applied.count, uecon.estimated_savings, quant.profile.selected. Migration notes: operators can revert to previous defaults via console or disable at route-level config. See release_notes for user-facing summary.
